reason: Selected controlled training results favor a strong SFT baseline and mixed-data transfer, without compute-normalized claims.

candidates.title: Include LoRA supervised tuning as a tool-calling baseline
candidates.rule: For Qwen3 tool-call adaptation with labeled calls, compare LoRA SFT with GRPO and sequential SFT-to-GRPO before assuming RL is the stronger training choice.
candidates.passage: achieving the best result in 15 of 18 settings
candidates.finding: LoRA SFT is strongest in fifteen of eighteen in-distribution settings across six Qwen3 sizes. GRPO wins more cross-dataset cells but its average advantage over SFT is under one point. Sequential training is rarely best.
candidates.conditions: Common formats, deduplicated fixed splits and controlled total example counts; the sequential method divides data between stages.
candidates.limitations: No compute-normalized comparison: GRPO uses more compute per example. One family and exact-match calls rather than long-horizon environment execution. LoRA-versus-full-tuning comparison is only at 4B.
candidates.validation_test: Compare methods on identical labels and deployed formats, recording training compute and exact-call plus execution success on in-distribution and transferred tasks.

candidates.title: Test mixed tool-call data when deployment spans formats
candidates.rule: For agents expected to handle diverse tool-call distributions, compare a balanced mixture of training corpora with single-corpus specialization on every intended target.
candidates.passage: The uniform mixture provides the strongest overall deployment choice
candidates.finding: The mixture remains within one to five points of the best dataset-specialized model on each target and avoids the observed poor Glaive-to-xLAM transfer across the tested scales and methods.
candidates.conditions: Seeded mixture samples up to twenty thousand examples per corpus, with fixed validation and test splits after deduplication.
candidates.limitations: A larger or more diverse mixture can change training cost; this does not isolate diversity at every equal-compute or equal-example budget. Results do not show that uniform weights suit every deployment.
candidates.validation_test: Compare specialized and mixed datasets at matched sample and compute budgets; weight target evaluations by actual deployment needs and check rare tools and no-tool requests.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
